title: Self-determination
html: The other day I had to visit my physician about something. After describing his diagnosis of my malady, the physician then went into 3 different treatment alternatives, ending with “So, what do you think you want to do?” His query reminded me of a great case on informed consent, Matthies v Mastromonaco, 733 A.2d 456 (1999). I wrote this case up for this column 27 years ago (Am J Orthod Dentofacial Orthop 1999;116:591-3), but after rereading it, I said to myself, “I gotta do this one again.” The reason was 2-fold: yes, it is a great teaching case for you guys and gals concerning informed consent, but it also provided me with the opportunity to measure my “personal and professional growth,” or lack of it, concerning this facet of orthodontic risk management.
